1.explanation: The root cause of the bug is in how the Dropdown component (packages/react/src/components/Dropdown/Dropdown.js) manages ARIA attributes and renders items for assistive technologies. The bug is likely due to a duplication of accessible labels or roles being applied to dropdown items or the menu in a way that causes screen readers to read both the item label and a redundant label (such as both the button and menu item text). The Dropdown class and function are responsible for rendering the dropdown, setting up accessibility attributes, and handling focus and keyboard navigation. Fixing the bug would require editing this class/function to ensure proper ARIA usage so that each dropdown item is only announced once by screen readers. The supporting components (ListBox, ListBoxMenuItem) are less likely to be the direct cause, since they mainly handle rendering wrappers and not accessibility logic, but may need minor adjustments if the fix involves changing how props are passed or how ARIA attributes are applied.
1.bug_scenario: The bug occurs when using Mac VoiceOver to navigate dropdown items in the Carbon Design System's Dropdown component. As shown in the image, when moving focus from one dropdown item to the next, VoiceOver reads each item twice (e.g., 'Option 4 Option 4, selected (5 of 6)'), instead of just once. This suggests duplicate information is being presented to assistive technologies, leading to a confusing user experience and violating accessibility best practices.
